articles.title: Oversight Board says Meta's rules for AI deepfakes are 'consistently and fundamentally inadequate' - Engadget
articles.text:
Oversight Board says Meta's rules for AI deepfakes are 'consistently and fundamentally inadequate'
The group has repeatedly criticized the company's handling of AI-generated material.
The Oversight Board is once again pushing Meta to address the flood of AI-generated content on its platform. The group published its two latest decisions dealing with the social media company's handling of AI content. The cases show that Meta's rules are "consistently and fundamentally inadequate to address the rapid rise of AI-generated content on its platforms," the board said in a statement.
Both cases were related to posts with AI-generated videos. One depicted a Scottish politician saying "refugees are welcome here, even if they rape our women, because white people do that too." The video was a "realistic" but synthetic portrayal, according to the Board. And the politician whose voice was replicated said the effect of the video was "quite traumatic."
Meta told the board that it didn't remove the video when it was reported because it hadn't been flagged by any of its "trusted partner" organizations and because it didn't seem to be interfering with voting or other processes. The video was also not labeled as AI-generated, apparently because the person who posted it didn't choose to disclose it was made with AI.
The Oversight Board said that the video should have been removed for breaking Meta's hateful conduct rules, and that it should have been prominently labeled as AI. Following the board's decision, Meta said it would remove the video.
The other case also features an AI-generated video of a real person. The video was based on a TV interview with a volunteer who was promoting menstrual health education. Some time after the initial interview, "accounts across social media platforms digitally manipulated the interview footage to ridicule her" and those videos went viral.
According to the board, Meta automatically closed a report and subsequent appeal about the post, which was never labeled as AI-generated. Meta removed harassing comments on the post for breaking its rules around bullying only after the Oversight Board got involved. In a statement following the board's decision, Meta said it would remove the post.
The group says that both cases highlight how AI content is being used to target people on its platforms and that the lack of consistent labeling is causing additional harm. "From politicians to private citizens, AI-generated deepfakes are increasingly being used to harass and silence women from engaging in public discourse," Oversight Board Co-Chair Pamela San Martin said in a statement. "These cases demonstrate a broader, troubling pattern in which women who engage publicly on issues are disproportionately subjected to harassment and misinformation."
The Oversight Board's criticism is unsurprising. The group, which makes policy recommendations to Meta, has repeatedly criticized the company for its approach to AI content and urged for new rules. The bigger question is whether Meta really cares about the board's perspective on this issue. The company has so far made few changes to its AI labels, which typically consist of a small banner that says "AI Info." The company hasn't agreed to implement many of the board's recommendations on AI labeling in other recent cases.
In its statements in response to the Oversight Board, Meta didn't address its criticism directly. But the company has 60 days to respond to its latest recommendations, including that it prioritize likely AI content for review when it's reported.
Update, September 17, 2026, 1:33PM ET: This post was updated to reflect Meta's responses to the Oversight Board.

articles.title: Pinterest launches Visual Search Ads for advertisers
articles.text:
“Traditional search advertising has long relied on keywords, but in an AI-driven world, people are expressing themselves in much richer ways,” said Bill Ready, chief executive of Pinterest.
The company announced Visual Search Ads on 17 September at Pinterest Presents, its annual advertiser summit. The format places advertisers in Pinterest search results and in Pin closeups.
Advertisers can bid for a top response and send people straight to their own site. The ads support lower-funnel objectives and work with Performance+, the company’s AI advertising suite.
The format goes into beta for eligible advertisers in every Pinterest ad market in the coming weeks, Pinterest said.
Eighty billion searches a month
Pinterest users run more than 80 billion searches a month, according to company data from its second-quarter earnings. The vast majority are visual and more than half are commercial.
Ready said more than 96% of those searches are unbranded, in remarks at the summit. People arrive with intent but before they have decided what to buy, he said.
He also said Pinterest has 640 million monthly users, that it has set user records for 12 straight quarters, and that Gen Z is now more than half its audience. In May, TNW reported that the company had crossed $1bn in quarterly revenue on the same search bet.
More tools for advertisers
Performance+ is adding Priority Products, which lets advertisers pick the products to push during a seasonal launch or a promotion. Pinterest is also adding self-serve A/B testing for creative, targeting and Performance+ campaigns.
App Promotion, an objective built for app installs, is now in global beta with qualified advertisers. One advertiser saw “up to an 85% improvement in cost per install” against previous workarounds, the company said.
That figure comes from a single US enterprise advertiser in an alpha test, Pinterest’s own footnote says. It covers August 2025 to August 2026.
Restyle and Pinterest Intelligence
Restyle, a consumer feature, is launching in beta in the US and Canada. It lets people photograph a room, then test and compare options in their own home.
Users can prompt the AI to add wall art, furniture or plants, change paint colour and lighting, or swap and erase individual items, TechCrunch reported. They can also ask for a different style, such as bohemian or industrial.
Restyle is an early preview for now and rolls out more widely next month, according to TechCrunch. Pinterest says the feature runs on Pinterest Intelligence, its visual understanding of images, products, taste and intent.
Pinterest said on Monday that Pinterest Intelligence combines Nvidia Blackwell GPUs and Nvidia Dynamo with open-source models and its own technology.
Ads inside AI products
The summit also brought back Bring My Pinterest to Life, a connected TV series, for a second season. Creators Tay BeepBoop Nakamoto and Caroline Vazzana return.
Other platforms are placing ads at the point of decision too. OpenAI is testing Sponsored Agents in ChatGPT. On Prime Day, AI assistants beat search at its own game.
Pinterest is changing its advertising model while a US judge puts Google’s ad tech business under a monitor. Its chief financial officer, Julia Donnelly, announced her departure on 31 August.

articles.title: PNJ xoay vốn nghìn tỷ, muốn trả tiền sớm cho khách giữa bốn bề sức ép
articles.text:
Rút ngắn thời gian thanh toán cho khách bán lại
CTCP Vàng bạc Đá quý Phú Nhuận (PNJ) vừa công bố nghị quyết HĐQT thông qua chủ trương điều chỉnh giảm thời gian thanh toán so với quy định hiện hành khi công ty mua lại sản phẩm từ khách hàng.
PNJ chưa công bố chi tiết phương án mới. Theo phương án trước đó, doanh nghiệp kéo dài thời gian thanh toán lên tối đa 120 ngày, chia thành 5 đợt. Nghị quyết mới cho biết việc điều chỉnh sẽ được áp dụng khác nhau theo từng dòng sản phẩm, trên cơ sở cân đối với tình hình tài chính thực tế của doanh nghiệp.
Ở diễn biến khác, bà Trần Phương Ngọc Thảo, Phó Chủ tịch HĐQT PNJ và là con gái Chủ tịch Cao Thị Ngọc Dung, bán 7 triệu cổ phiếu PNJ trong ngày 11/9 theo phương thức thỏa thuận.
Sau giao dịch, bà Thảo còn hơn 11 triệu cổ phiếu, tương đương 2,15% vốn điều lệ. Nếu tính theo giá đóng cửa 37.300 đồng/cp hôm đó, số cổ phiếu bán ra có giá trị khoảng 261 tỷ đồng.
Trước đó, bà Thảo và em gái Trần Phương Ngọc Hà cũng đăng ký bán tổng cộng 25 triệu cổ phiếu PNJ nhằm tạo nguồn vốn để bà Cao Thị Ngọc Dung cho PNJ vay, bổ sung vốn lưu động và phục vụ hoạt động sản xuất kinh doanh. Khoản vay có hạn mức tối đa không quá 5% tổng tài sản PNJ tại báo cáo tài chính gần nhất, tương đương khoảng 1.080 tỷ đồng theo quy mô tài sản cuối tháng 6/2026; không có tài sản bảo đảm, thời hạn tối đa 12 tháng và có thể giải ngân nhiều đợt.
Đây là nguồn vốn được PNJ thu xếp trong bối cảnh doanh nghiệp đang xử lý lượng hàng hóa khách hàng bán lại và điều chỉnh chính sách thu đổi.
Sau những thông tin liên quan vụ án buôn lậu kim cương tại Thanh Hóa và việc một số cá nhân liên quan Công ty TNHH MTV Giám định PNJ (PNJ-LAB) bị khởi tố, PNJ đối mặt với việc khách hàng bán lại kim cương, trang sức. PNJ từng áp dụng chính sách thanh toán trong 120 ngày hoặc hướng khách hàng chuyển đổi sang sản phẩm khác.
Theo báo cáo tài chính bán niên sau soát xét, lợi nhuận sau thuế hợp nhất 6 tháng đầu năm 2026 của PNJ giảm từ hơn 1.184 tỷ đồng xuống còn 728,5 tỷ đồng, chủ yếu liên quan đến các khoản dự phòng và ước tính chi phí trong chính sách thu đổi hàng hóa.
PNJ ghi nhận tổng cộng khoảng 3.684 tỷ đồng dự phòng, trong đó 2.267,3 tỷ đồng liên quan chính sách thu đổi hàng hóa và 1.416,8 tỷ đồng là dự phòng giảm giá hàng tồn kho.
Với hàng hóa bán từ năm 2019 trở về trước, giá trị đưa vào cơ sở tính toán hơn 10.137 tỷ đồng, tỷ lệ khách hàng quay lại bán được giả định ở mức 7%, tương ứng tổn thất dự kiến khoảng 183,2 tỷ đồng. Đây là các cơ sở để ước tính nghĩa vụ và tổn thất, không đồng nghĩa toàn bộ số tiền trên là khoản PNJ chắc chắn phải chi ra.
Cổ phiếu ở vùng giá thấp, triển vọng chưa rõ ràng
Kết thúc phiên sáng 16/9, PNJ giảm 300 đồng xuống 36.900 đồng/cp, thanh khoản đạt gần 1,38 triệu cổ phiếu. Khối ngoại bán 488.000 cổ phiếu, trong khi mua vào 87.300 đơn vị.
Từ vùng đáy quanh 30.000 đồng/cp hồi tháng 7, PNJ có thời điểm phục hồi lên vùng 43.000 đồng/cp vào cuối tháng 8 (tương đương khoảng 43%) trước khi giảm trở lại 36.900 đồng/cp. So với mức đỉnh khoảng 85.000 đồng/cp hồi đầu năm, thị giá hiện thấp hơn khoảng 56%. Diễn biến này cho thấy đà hồi phục chưa tạo được xu hướng tăng ổn định.
Ở chiều mua vào, Tổng giám đốc Phan Quốc Công đã mua thành công 1 triệu cổ phiếu PNJ trong giai đoạn từ ngày 31/7 đến 14/8, nâng sở hữu lên 0,2% vốn điều lệ. Trong khi đó, ông Cao Ngọc Duy, em trai bà Cao Thị Ngọc Dung, mua thêm 300.000 cổ phiếu.
Một số tổ chức nước ngoài cũng gia tăng sở hữu. Nhóm quỹ do Sprucegrove Investment Management quản lý mua thêm khoảng 1,62 triệu cổ phiếu ngày 14/8, nâng tỷ lệ sở hữu lên 5,04%. Ngày 19/8, nhóm nhà đầu tư liên quan T. Rowe Price Associates mua thêm hơn 4,85 triệu cổ phiếu, nâng tỷ lệ sở hữu từ 5,07% lên 6,02%.
Ở chiều ngược lại, Dragon Capital và VinaCapital đã giảm tỷ lệ sở hữu tại PNJ trong các giao dịch trước đó, trong đó VinaCapital đã xuống dưới ngưỡng 5%.
Về kinh doanh, doanh thu thuần hợp nhất 6 tháng đầu năm đạt hơn 25.709 tỷ đồng, tăng khoảng 49%, nhưng lợi nhuận sau thuế sau soát xét chỉ còn 728,5 tỷ đồng, giảm khoảng 35% so với cùng kỳ. Việc doanh thu tăng mạnh nhưng lợi nhuận giảm sâu cho thấy biên lợi nhuận và chất lượng tăng trưởng đang là vấn đề đáng chú ý của PNJ trong năm nay.
Doanh thu tăng mạnh trong bối cảnh nhóm vàng 24K đóng góp đáng kể, trong khi biên lợi nhuận của nhóm này thấp hơn hoạt động bán lẻ trang sức. Vì vậy, cơ cấu doanh thu và khả năng phục hồi của mảng trang sức bán lẻ là những yếu tố cần theo dõi trong các quý tới.
Vì vậy, câu chuyện của PNJ tới đây không chỉ nằm ở việc bổ sung vốn lưu động. Doanh nghiệp còn phải xử lý các khoản dự phòng lớn, thực hiện chính sách thu đổi, củng cố niềm tin của khách hàng và cải thiện chất lượng lợi nhuận.
Một mốc đáng chú ý là Đại hội đồng cổ đông bất thường dự kiến diễn ra ngày 21/10/2026 tại TPHCM. PNJ dự kiến trình cổ đông các chỉ tiêu kinh doanh điều chỉnh cho năm 2026 và định hướng hoạt động giai đoạn tiếp theo. Đây có thể là dịp doanh nghiệp làm rõ hơn kế hoạch xử lý các vấn đề phát sinh, nhu cầu vốn và định hướng kinh doanh trong thời gian tới.

articles.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Side Events schedule: NMI, Backblaze, PeakXV Partners, Augment, and more to host | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TechCrunch Disrupt is where the tech community comes together to build, debate, and connect. And while the main event takes over Moscone West from October 13-15, the conversation doesn’t stop when the Expo Hall closes.
The TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Side Event program brings founders, investors, operators, researchers, and tech enthusiasts together across San Francisco for panels, workshops, networking events, parties, and more.
The schedule is growing, with more events being added in the lead-up to Disrupt. Whether you’re looking to meet other founders, connect with investors, dig into a specific technology, or simply spend more time with the tech community, there’s plenty happening around Disrupt.
Check the chronological schedule regularly as new Side Events are added weekly.
Featured Side Events
A few of this year’s Side Events are hosted by TechCrunch partners, bringing the companies and communities behind some of the biggest conversations in tech into the Disrupt Week experience.
Serve, Swipe, & Settle: Mixer for SaaS leaders scaling into embedded payments
October 12 | 5:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m. PT
Join SaaS founders, developers, and technical leaders at SPIN San Francisco for conversations about turning embedded payments into a revenue stream. Over Ping-Pong, food, and drinks, compare notes on monetization, brand control, and scaling beyond basic payments.
Hosted by: NMI
RSVP↗
The Afterburn: TechCrunch Disrupt Edition
October 14 | 6:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m. PT
Take a break from the pitching, demoing, and networking at this evening mixer. Join founders, builders, investors, and other members of the tech community for cocktails, appetizers, and conversation.
No panels or presentations, just a chance to connect and unwind after a day at TechCrunch Disrupt.
Hosted by: Backblaze and Flamethrower
RSVP↗
Ecosystem Mixer
October 14 | 5:30 p.m. – 8:30 p.m. PT
Join Peak XV for a mixer with founders, operators, and investors building what’s next. Good drinks, better conversations, zero pitches required to join our mixer.
Hosted by: PeakXV Partners
RSVP↗
Liquid Assets: A Private Markets Cocktail Party
October 14 | 5:30 p.m. – 8:30 p.m. PT
Disrupt is three days of panels. This is not one of them.
Augment and Mintz are hosting a cocktail party Wednesday evening with drinks, light bites, and plenty of room for conversation. No programming or preset meetings, just an opportunity to connect with people across the private markets, technology, and venture ecosystem.
Hosted by: Augment and Mintz
RSVP↗

5:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m.

7:00 p.m. – 8:30 p.m.

SF Exclusive VIP Drinks for AI Founders & Accredited Investors

Harvard Griffin GSAS Alumni Networking Mixer
5:30 p.m. – 7:30 p.m.

South Asian Investor Founder Connect: TechCrunch Disrupt
5:30 p.m. – 7:30 p.m.

Content Creators Meetup @ TechCrunch Disrupt

Explore how AI companies turn inference costs into business value, with conversation around model selection, routing, caching, reliability, pricing, and connecting token spend to revenue and customer outcomes.
AI Made Every Candidate Look Perfect. How Do You Find the Real Ones?
6:30 p.m. – 8:30 p.m.
When AI can polish every résumé, profile, and interview answer, how do you identify meaningful signal? Join founders, investors, and operators for an intimate conversation about evaluating talent in an AI-first world.
SignalFire’s Disrupt Week Arthaus After-Party
7:00 p.m. – 11:00 p.m.
SignalFire’s annual Disrupt Week after-party returns with live music, immersive art and technology installations, food and drinks, and a gathering of founders, investors, journalists, and builders.
Thursday, October 15

5:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m.
A rooftop happy hour for SaaS and AI founders, C-suite leaders, investors, and tech media. Attendance is limited and guests are screened in advance.
Korea Emerging Tech Showcase
5:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m.
Discover emerging technology startups from Korea spanning AI, software, medtech, clean tech, digital platforms, and advanced industrial solutions. The evening features rapid-fire pitches followed by networking with founders, investors, and global partners.
LP, GP & Funded Founder Networking
5:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m.
An intimate networking event bringing together LPs, GPs, and funded founders for conversations around technology, venture capital, and the future of the industry.
Fynex x Orion VC | Curated Rooftop Party
6:00 p.m. – 9:00 p.m.
A curated rooftop gathering for founders and operators building with AI and investors focused on AI and infrastructure. Expect food, drinks, and an approval-only guest list designed for meaningful conversations.
Side Event Guidelines and Disclaimers

- A Side Event RSVP does not grant access to TechCrunch Disrupt. Side Events are separate from TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, which takes place October 13-15 at Moscone West. You’ll need a valid Disrupt pass or badge to attend the main event.
- Side Events are independently operated. Each event is organized and operated solely by its listed host and is not organized, operated, or sponsored by TechCrunch or its affiliates unless explicitly stated otherwise.
- Age requirements vary. All Side Events are 18+ unless otherwise specified. Some venues and events may be restricted to guests 21 and older.
- Side Events are generally open to the public. Individual hosts may have their own guest lists, capacity limits, approval requirements, or other restrictions, so check the event details before attending.
- RSVPs are required where indicated. Please register for each Side Event directly through the RSVP link provided. An RSVP does not guarantee entry if an event reaches capacity or the host has additional admission requirements.
- Event details may change. Hosts are responsible for their individual event details, including timing, location, programming, and admission requirements. Check the RSVP page for the latest information before heading out.
More Side Events will be added as we get closer to Disrupt. To see what’s happening and when, the chronological schedule is your friend. It has the full lineup, organized by date and time.

articles.title: Your robotaxi might be a narc
articles.text:
In early September, two teenagers got into a Waymo, but then ended up in the back of a police car. The robotaxi company said it detected “a violation of our terms of service involving a firearm,” pulled the car over, and alerted emergency services, according to the Los Angeles Times. Police arrested the passengers after allegedly finding a loaded AR-style “ghost gun” in the vehicle.
Your robotaxi might be a narc
Waymo notified the police when it detected a gun during a ride, leading to the arrest of two teenagers. The incident exposes the limits of privacy in an autonomous vehicle.
Your robotaxi might be a narc
Waymo notified the police when it detected a gun during a ride, leading to the arrest of two teenagers. The incident exposes the limits of privacy in an autonomous vehicle.
The arrests exposed a lot of unanswered questions about privacy and autonomous vehicles, including what they are recording, what they do with the footage, and how much privacy riders should expect while riding inside them.
Waymo’s camera-covered cars have already been drawn into the debate over privacy and surveillance. On a number of occasions, law enforcement agencies have obtained search warrants for footage captured by its cars, according to Bloomberg. Last year, the LAPD obtained footage of a hit-and-run that was recorded by a nearby Waymo vehicle. During anti-ICE protests in Los Angeles, five Waymos were vandalized and set on fire amid questions about whether the vehicles could be capturing images of protesters that might be used as evidence to identify or arrest them. Waymo does not publicly disclose how many law enforcement requests it receives or how often it complies.
Those concerns echo the backlash against Flock’s network of automated license-plate readers, which have given police the ability to track cars across jurisdictions and have prompted growing fears about government surveillance and misuse. Unlike fixed Flock cameras, Waymos move through cities carrying cameras both outside and inside their vehicles.
The latest case of the arrested teens takes those concerns a step further. Police did not approach Waymo after a crime looking for footage its cameras happened to capture. Waymo detected something inside the car and initiated the police response itself.
Waymo spokesperson Julia Ilina told The Verge in an email that the company uses its internal cameras to help enforce its terms of service, including detecting prohibited items and behavior. She said it uses automated technology to help Waymo’s teams identify potential violations, such as the presence of firearms inside the vehicle. “If Waymo detects a firearm in the vehicle, we may reach out to local law enforcement,” she added.
Waymo did not explain how its automated system determines whether something may be a firearm, how confident it has to be before something gets flagged, what role humans play between an automated alert and a call to police, or what other violations of its terms of service might prompt a police response. Those are important omissions. This wasn’t a human taxi driver deciding to call 911. It was a driverless car, equipped with cameras and an AI brain, escalating a situation involving its passengers to police.
Bob Somers, a former engineer at autonomous vehicle company Zoox and technical adviser to the AV-safety nonprofit SAVE-US, said he would expect Waymo’s system to look for a range of potentially dangerous weapons and behaviors. The software may not need to decide with certainty that it has seen a firearm. It could instead flag something that resembles one for further review, he said.
“If there is a certain set of objects detected, then that would probably loop in a remote operator to take a look at what’s going on,” Somers said.
Phil Koopman, a Carnegie Mellon University professor emeritus who researches autonomous vehicle safety, said computer vision systems can be trained to recognize objects and potentially dangerous situations.
“If there is a certain set of objects detected, then that would probably loop in a remote operator to take a look at what’s going on.”
— Bob Somers
“If you can train a computer to look at the road and decide how to drive, you can train a computer to decide if somebody’s holding a gun,” Koopman said. But, he added, those systems are “never 100 percent accurate.”
That’s where the unanswered question about human review becomes important.
A human taxi driver who sees a passenger holding something has context. They’ve been in the car for the entire ride. They can hear what the passengers are saying and ask questions. They can decide whether the object is a real gun, a toy, or something else entirely. Back in July, Waymo reported two teens to the police for underage drinking and shooting a toy gun loaded with water beads from the vehicle. It was not clear whether the teens ultimately faced any charges.
A remote worker brought in to review a flagged moment might not have all of that context because they haven’t experienced the entire ride the way a human driver would. Waymo says its interior microphones are generally active only during calls with Rider Support or when riders enable them, meaning a reviewer may not be able to hear what preceded the flagged moment. As of earlier this year, Waymo has about 70 “remote assistance agents” on duty at a given time in the US and the Philippines, who “provide advice and support to the Waymo Driver but do not directly control, steer, or drive the vehicle.” Waymo has not said whether the people reviewing possible violations inside its cars are among those agents.
“It’s really important that Waymo gets it right when they alert the police to something dangerous,” Koopman said. Beyond undermining riders’ trust in robotaxis, a false alarm could put passengers at risk during a police encounter.
Then there’s the question of what Waymo tells riders to expect. Without a driver in the front seat, robotaxis can feel more private than they actually are. In 2023, the San Francisco Standard spoke with four people who said they had hooked up or had sex in Cruise robotaxis, despite the cameras inside them. The publication could not find anyone who said they had done so in a Waymo, but the episodes illustrate how readily passengers can mistake the absence of a human driver for the absence of a witness.
Waymo’s terms of service requires riders to comply with applicable laws and prohibits them from creating a dangerous condition, carrying weapons “or anything that resembles a weapon, e.g. toy gun,” or using drugs. Riders must be at least 18 to ride alone in San Francisco. The two riders arrested this month allegedly violated both the age and weapons restrictions.
The terms say Waymo can suspend or terminate a rider’s access if it believes the rider has violated the rules. Earlier this year, Waymo suspended the account used to book a ride after three boys were photographed hanging out the windows of the vehicle and taking selfies. But they do not plainly tell passengers that the company may call the police based on what it sees inside the car.
“It’s really important that Waymo gets it right when they alert the police to something dangerous.”
— Phil Koopman
Waymo’s public camera policy says its interior cameras can be used to “check that in-car rules are being followed” and “promote safety and security.” It says Waymo Support may review recorded video after an issue is brought to the company’s attention and, in urgent circumstances, access live video during a trip.
The policy also says Waymo may share certain data with law enforcement as needed to comply with legal requirements, enforce agreements, or protect the safety of riders and others. But it doesn’t specify that automated monitoring inside the vehicle may trigger Waymo itself to contact police.
Hayley Tsukayama, director of state affairs at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, called Waymo’s public policies “very broad.” Riders shouldn’t have to infer from language about “safety and security” that their behavior could result in a police response, she said, adding that Waymo should clearly disclose that possibility before passengers get into the car.
“I’m not condoning illegal behavior in rideshares,” she said, but “if they’re going to share it with authorities, then that should be clearly stated in the policy.” As it stands, Tsukayama said, “it is outside of the expectations of consumers.”
Then again, robotaxis themselves are outside the norm. As they become more common, riders may have to develop a new set of expectations about what happens inside them. A human driver can decide how to respond to what happens in their car. In a robotaxi, cameras and software can flag what happens inside, remote workers may become involved, and the vehicle can pull over while police are summoned.
Waymo’s system may have helped police recover an illegal firearm in this case. But the incident also raises a more basic question about what kind of space a robotaxi is: a ride with cameras for safety, a continuously monitored space, or a system that can call the cops on its own passengers.
That question is already showing up in fiction. Robotaxis are making their debut as villains in Road Rage, an upcoming short film about a driverless car that turns against humans. One of the film’s more unsettling ideas is that a robotaxi could end up acting less like transportation and more like law enforcement. This month offered a glimpse of what that might look like.

articles.title: An iOS 27 bug can temporarily freeze your iPhone - Engadget
articles.text:
An iOS 27 bug can temporarily freeze your iPhone
Here’s how to fix it.
If you're here because your newly updated iPhone suddenly froze while you were using it, don't panic. There's an iOS 27 bug that can temporarily freeze your phone if you happen to do a series of swipes. As 9to5Mac notes, it's not going to ruin your device permanently, and you can get out of by doing a force restart. A force reboot is the first thing you should do when you're troubleshooting issues with any device, as it will clear your RAM and close programs that could be causing you problems.
Since your iPhone is frozen, and you can't access the power icon, you'll have to press and quickly release the volume up button and then do the same with the volume down button. Afterward, press and hold the side button until the Apple logo appears, and you know your phone is going through a restart. Take note that you may have to press on that button for more than 10 seconds.
In case you haven't encountered the bug yet and were wondering how it's triggered, it's by swiping down the Notification Center and the Control Center in quick succession. You'll then see buttons and icons stuck at the top of the screen, and you'll find your iPhone unable to register your swipes and taps. Apple will likely roll out a fix for this in the future, but for now, you may want to memorize our instructions for force restarts above.

articles.title: Apple will let EU apps use less-alarming tracking-consent screens | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As a result of a multi-year antitrust probe by Germany’s federal competition regulator and others, Apple has agreed to modify the requirements for apps on its platforms that ask for consent to track the user across other apps or websites.
Regulators said this system, known as App Tracking Transparency, or ATT, had favored Apple over third-party apps, since Apple allows its own apps to use consumers’ data from its ecosystem without requiring a consent screen.
The new agreements with select European competition authorities don’t do away with the need to prompt users, or when that prompt is to be shown. Instead, they allow app developers whose software is distributed in the EU to display an alternative consent screen that includes modified formatting, language, and the option to link out to “additional information” about why the app is requesting this permission, among other things.
Apple’s compliance involves over half-a-dozen changes that attempt to make these ATT consent screens less scary to end users. This includes showing them as full-page screens, not pop-ups; removing the word “track”; changing the choice buttons to “Allow” and “Reject” instead of “Allow” and “Ask App Not to Track”; changing the colors and formatting; and more. Plus, developers can offer users more detailed information through a clickable link, explaining how they use this data and why it’s being requested.
The iPhone maker says that, due to legal requirements, only the alternative version of the system prompt will be available to apps distributed in Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and Romania.
Users typically respond to consent screens by asking apps not to track them, which hurts ad-supported businesses, like Meta, while boosting Apple’s own. In short, the apps asking for such permissions do so because it lets them show personalized advertising, which generates more revenue, helping the app developer to make money.
Apple, however, argued that these consent screens help protect consumer privacy, even though it permits its own apps to display personalized ads based on the data they collect from its ecosystem.
The company said it will now allow app developers distributing to the EU to re-prompt their EU users one year after the user’s previous choice in their ATT consent screen.

articles.title: Nvidia's Huang expects to sell twice as many chips next year
articles.text:
Jensen Huang told reporters at King Charles III’s AI summit in Scotland that he expects to sell twice as many chips in the coming year. Nvidia’s own August guidance was 70% revenue growth, with a doubling described as what the company could reach if it had enough supply.
Jensen Huang expects to sell twice as many chips in the coming year, he told reporters at an event convened by King Charles III in Scotland, Bloomberg reported. He put it down to AI spreading across industries.
That is a larger number than his own company has guided to.
Last month Nvidia forecast 70% revenue growth for its next fiscal year. Finance chief Colette Kress said the company was supply constrained, and that revenue could double if it were not.
Units and revenue are different measures, and the distance between the two is the story.
Nvidia posted $96.2B in revenue for the quarter to 26 July, more than double the same period last year, and guided to $108B for the current one. Doubling the number of chips it ships means capacity that does not exist yet.
Which raises the question of who is at the front of the queue.
Europe is planning up to seven AI gigafactories, and it will be buying on the open market. The Commission has budgeted around EUR 30B in total, of which roughly EUR 1B of the public share is committed. The tender call went out on 30 July.
Nvidia takes about that much in data centre revenue in a day.
The Commission’s own figure is around 100,000 chips for each gigafactory, four times what an AI factory holds. Construction on the first starts in 2027 and the sites are meant to be running from 2028. Seventy-seven proposals came in from 16 member states across 60 sites.
Huang’s doubling, if it happens, happens before any of that is switched on.
He spent the rest of the afternoon on safety. At the same summit he argued that AI should not be regulated like social media, because it is a technology underneath products rather than a product itself.
He also said an unsafe product should be held back and engineered further. Around 30 executives, policymakers and researchers were in the room. Industry figures there had raised slowing development down.
Nvidia shares rose as much as 2.8% in New York and are up about 17% this year. The chips Europe is counting on for 2028 come out of the same order book.
